title: Surjective closed immersions: module equivalence and finite local models
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring and $h:T\hookrightarrow Y$ a surjective closed immersion of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-surjective-morphism]. Work on either the small étale or the small pro-étale sites [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], with compatible universes and ordinary module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] over the constant ring sheaves $A_Y,A_T$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Inverse image $h^*=h^{-1}$ uses the canonical identification $h^{-1}A_Y\cong A_T$, and $h_*$ has its induced $A_Y$-action [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image, def-weil-pbc-direct-image, def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. The actual adjunction unit and counit are natural isomorphisms
$$H\xrightarrow{\sim}h_*h^*H,\qquad h^*h_*N\xrightarrow{\sim}N$$
for every module sheaf $H$ on $Y$ and $N$ on $T$. Thus $h^*$ and $h_*$ are quasi-inverse equivalences of module-sheaf categories. For every $A$-module $M$, $h^*\underline M_Y\cong\underline M_T$. A module sheaf $H$ on $Y$ is finite locally constant if and only if $h^*H$ is: here this means that on a covering family of the indicated site it is isomorphic to constant module sheaves with finite $A$-module models [def-constructible-locally-constant, def-weil-proetale-locally-constant-sheaf]. The same equivalence holds with the additional requirement that every local model be a direct summand of a finite free $A$-module. No Noetherianity or uniform nilpotence bound is assumed.

proof.text: A surjective closed immersion, and every base change of it, is a universal homeomorphism. Apply the published ModuleCat-valued upperStar/lowerStar topological-invariance APIs on both sites. In the etale case these immediately give the actual adjunction unit and counit. The pro-etale fixed-module equivalence is used below to establish the intrinsic module adjunction.

Restrict intrinsic pro-etale constant-ring modules to constant scalars via proEtaleModuleRestriction_isEquivalence. The directImageComparison from the pullback-encoding module identifies intrinsic pushforward followed by scalar restriction with fixed-module pushforward. Cancel the scalar restriction equivalence to prove that the stipulated intrinsic pushforward is an equivalence. Its actual normalized adjunction then gives equivalence of the stipulated pullback and invertibility of the actual unit and counit.

Use the proved ConstantScalarComparison restriction, full-faithfulness and constantComparisonHom_isIso helpers from the constructibility-encoding module, both globally and on the slice site. The locally bijective constant-ring sheafification unit supplies their hypotheses. The pro-etale slice equivalence, its constant-sheaf comparison and upperStarIsoLocalizationRestriction convert localized intrinsic constant-model isomorphisms into fixed-module inverse-image isomorphisms and back. Rewrite the cover at the terminal site object as a scheme pro-etale cover, retaining the identical model predicate.

proof.text: Etale constants use upperStarConstantSheafIso. For fixed-module pro-etale constants, compose the comparison with the standard sheafPullback construction and constantSheafsheafPullbackIso. Compose this with the intrinsic/fixed-module pullback comparison and the scalar constant-module comparison, and lift the resulting isomorphism through fully faithful scalar restriction. This proves the required intrinsic constant-module clause for every module, without assuming its finiteness.

proof.text: Preservation on each site pulls back the trivializing cover. upperStarComp and the pullback-square identity compare the two iterated inverse images. Pull back each model isomorphism and compose with the constant-sheaf comparison. Convert to and from the localized-site presentation using the etale or pro-etale slice equivalence. Reuse every model, its finiteness proof, and its finite-free splitting. The pro-etale statement is proved first for an arbitrary predicate P on the models.

source.place: lemma-pullback-locally-constant; sites.tex Tag 00YV (proposition-functoriality-algebraic-structures-topoi), localized inverse images

proof.text: Etale reflection proved in Lean: lift each member of a trivializing cover on T through h.Etale.objPreimage and objObjPreimageIso. The lifted objects cover Y: lift a point y to T by surjectivity of h, lift it to an original cover member, apply the inverse site-object isomorphism, and project the resulting point of the fiber product to the lifted object over Y. Pull back its given model isomorphism along the site-object isomorphism. upperStarComp and the cartesian-square identity identify its source with the base-changed pullback of H. Identify its target by upperStarConstantSheafIso. The first projection is a base-changed universal homeomorphism, so its ModuleCat-valued inverse image is fully faithful; preimageIso descends the model isomorphism. Convert back to the localized-site presentation. All models and splitting maps remain exactly the same.

source.place: Tag 04DZ (theorem-topological-invariance), Tag 03SI (proposition-topological-invariance); lifting module trivializations by full faithfulness

proof.text: Pro-etale reflection: restrict a given cover to a small indexing type and apply exists_cover_refinement_surjective_closed. Reindex its output into the required larger universe. For each member the supplied cartesian square makes q a surjective closed immersion. Pull the old model isomorphism back along r. upperStarComp, the cartesian-square identity and the refinement factorization identify its source with q* of the restriction of H, and the constant comparison identifies its target with q* of the same constant model. The published fixed-module topological-invariance equivalence for q gives preimageIso, descending the trivialization. No lift of every weakly etale object is asserted.

The etale proof likewise retains them. Empty covers and schemes, the zero ring and rank zero are included without additional assumptions.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q80-4227bccb2 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item in full: all 8 steps and the statements of all 21 cited nodes. I read the unit sk-lem-sf-flat-model and how the parent det-sf-flat-model-generation uses the item in clause (2). Sources read: Stacks 09AB (proetale.tex l.4962) and 04DZ (etale-cohomology.tex l.6354). The statement is unchanged and true: a surjective closed immersion is integral, universally injective and surjective. I tested it on id, Spec k→Spec k[ε], a nil but not nilpotent ideal, the empty scheme, the zero ring and the zero module. Step checks: (1) universal homeomorphism and base change, with étale and pro-étale invariance for the actual unit and counit. (2) The module unit equals the abelian unit (lem-pe), which equals the set unit (adjunction-lifting lemma); the coefficient maps are canonical. (3) The counit follows from the triangle identity and reflection of isomorphisms. (4) lem-sfb-geometric-inverse-image-constant-module states exactly the constant-module comparison used. (5) The graph pair is initial, so the colimit is H(W); pro-étale restriction uses the object-restriction lemma; covers are preserved by base change (fpqc for pro-étale). (6) and (7) Reflection works by lifting covers, or by the Lean cover-refinement node with r_b weakly étale, plus full faithfulness of the base-changed pullback. (8) The models are literally unchanged. The declared tool_uses are acceptable; the other off-unit citations are Mathlib leaves or closed in slopmaster2. No cycle, no new nodes, no duplicate: lemma-constructible-universal-homeomorphism-invariance and the condensed nodes are narrower or about different coefficients. Batch-5 check on lem-trf-proetale-topological-invariance: it is Stacks 09AB, a general pro-étale topological-invariance result. Neither the trace formula nor Poincaré duality gives it. Its full closure (1146 nodes) contains no other sec-trace-formula or sec-poincare-duality node, no batch-4 target and no nt-assume leaf. The item's pro-étale clauses genuinely need it, so I accept the citation as outside the assumed statements. No fixes.

lean.statement: theorem sfbEtale_surjectiveClosed_module_invariance {T Y : Scheme.{u}} (h : T ⟶ Y) [IsClosedImmersion h] [Surjective h] (A : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing A] [Finite A] : IsIso (Etale.upperStarLowerStarAdjunction (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) h).unit ∧ IsIso (Etale.upperStarLowerStarAdjunction (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) h).counit ∧ (Etale.upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) h).IsEquivalence ∧ (Etale.lowerStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) h).IsEquivalence ∧ (∀ M : ModuleCat.{u + 1} A, Nonempty ((Etale.upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) h).obj ((constantSheaf Y.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A)).obj M) ≅ (constantSheaf T.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A)).obj M)) ∧ (∀ (H : Sheaf Y.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A)) (projective : Bool), sfbEtaleFiniteLocalModels A H projective ↔ sfbEtaleFiniteLocalModels A ((Etale.upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) h).obj H) projective)
lean.note: Two theorem statements cover the etale and pro-etale clauses. The etale version uses the published fixed ModuleCat-valued presentation; the pro-etale version uses the recorded ordinary constant-ring module operations, with their actual normalized adjunction. The two finite-local-model helpers expand the local-model clauses of this node using existing localized constant sheaves; the Bool selects whether explicit finite-free retractions are required. No stalk-based replacement, etale-origin condition, Noetherian assumption, or uniform nilpotence bound.
